guard_adversarial_review.question: It is a heuristic, not a type checker. What does it STILL miss, and is it theatre or genuinely useful?
guard_adversarial_review.method: I copied scripts/check-numerals.mjs into a sandbox with a copy of dashboard.ts and ran 13 mutations: 1 control, 3 reverts of the round-19 defects, and 9 defects I wrote myself in the shapes this file actually uses.
guard_adversarial_review.controls_reproduce: Confirmed — clean tree exits 0; reverting the idle-hours fix, the LIST_CAP fix and the loss-count fix each exits 1. Your falsification claim is true.
defects_it_passes: D1 · a literal Latin digit inside Arabic copy — «الحد الأعلى 50 جهة». PASSES. The guard inspects concatenation SHAPE and never inspects string CONTENT. Live instances at aed03a3: :967 «50», :1147 «92%», KB_SECTIONS «3 عناصر» / «2 من 8» / «0 ملفات».

D2 · a plain numeric property — ' + d.added + ' جهة'. PASSES. NUMERIC only matches Math.round|floor|ceil|abs(, .length|.count|.score, and LIST_CAP. Live instances: :1162, :1209, :1230, :1231 — «أُضيف 128 حُدّث 34 غير صالح 6», which I rendered in the browser to confirm.
D3 · an arithmetic expression — ' + (agg.targeted - agg.replied) + ' متبقٍ'. PASSES.
D4 · a template literal — `${entities.length} جهة`. PASSES. There is no backtick rule at all.
D5 · a Latin % closing an unlisted tag — '92%'. PASSES. LATIN_PCT hardcodes and . Live instance: :1147, the exact line.

D6 · Number(n).toLocaleString('ar-SA-u-nu-latn') — renders LATIN digits through a call the guard reads as correct formatting. PASSES. This is not hypothetical: that exact locale was in this file until d44236f.

D7 · a UI concat on a line whose FIRST numeric concat is CSS. PASSES. re.exec finds only the first match; CSS_CTX then skips it and the rest of the line is never re-scanned. Nearly every line in this file mixes inline styles with values.

D8/D9 · any identifier ENDING in fmtN( — blankFormatted does indexOf('fmtN(') with no left boundary, so `Math.roundfmtN(x)` is rewritten to `Math.roundN` and matches nothing. This is not a hypothetical defect: it is THE defect this commit shipped, and the guard's own paren-counting improvement — added this round to fix a previous false negative — is what conceals it.

Also unguarded by construction: array indexing (c[1], r[1]), which the script excludes DELIBERATELY and documents as a noise trade-off. That documented exclusion is directly responsible for the four 26px Latin numbers on #kb/<product>.
guard_adversarial_review.score: 1 shape caught, 9 realistic shapes passed, and 4 of the 9 have live instances in the file it just declared clean.
guard_adversarial_review.ruling_real_or_theatre: Genuinely useful, and mis-labelled — which makes it dangerous in a specific, fixable way. Useful: it is a real regression lock on the exact shape that produced M4, it reproducibly fails on all three round-19 defects, it reads the SOURCE rather than the DOM (the correct insight), and it is wired ahead of fly deploy so it cannot be skipped. That is worth keeping. Dangerous: its success line asserts «every number in src/dashboard.ts routes through fmtN()», which is false at the commit that printed it, and that sentence became «S6 shipped… ONE numeral path» in the report to me. A check that claims a property it does not verify converts an unverified hope into a green tick that everyone downstream cites as proof — under user-model Rule 2 the guard's own output is a Rule-2 violation. The repair is cheap and I am ordering it, not deleting the guard: make the message state the shape checked, add the literal-Latin-digit-in-an-Arabic-string rule and the tag-agnostic % rule (three lines, catches :967 and :1147 today), fix blankFormatted's left boundary (one character: /(?<![\w$])fmtN\(/), and move the property-level assertion to smoke.py where the rendered DOM cannot lie.

scores.rationale: intent_fidelity 8 (held). Every specific must I wrote in round 19 was executed and I verified each under its own trigger condition, not by reading the diff: the idle-hours counter, LIST_CAP, the loss-cause count, the readiness ring, the import-validation count, the typo. That is a clean execution record and it deserves the 8. It is not 9 because the intent was «one numeral system on the screens my team will see», and a screen one click inside the demo path reads 2 Arabic-Indic to 38 Latin. completeness 7 (held, and the number is again a net of two real movements in opposite directions — I would rather say that than pretend it is a clean 7). Up: the bare-toLocaleString class is genuinely dead (1 remaining, inside fmtN, against 76 fmtN calls), the enforcement exists and is wired ahead of deploy, and — the part I want to credit loudest — round-19's STATE lesson was actually applied; all three conditional defects hold under their triggers. Down: the audited screen set did not grow for the fourth round, three of round-19's should-orders (:1162's import chips, the 375px column CSS, the «معرفة» collision) were not attempted, and a new class of latent site — literal Latin digits inside Arabic string constants — is untouched and unguarded. coherence 7 (down from 8, and this is the score that moved). Two reasons, both structural rather than aesthetic. First, the product contradicts itself on one screen: «٩٢٪» in the ring, «7 0 0 1» in 26px Latin below it, «جاهزية الأقسام — 92%» below that, and «0 ملفات» asserting no attachments 300px under a row showing the attached file's real name. Second, the build now asserts a property it does not hold — the deploy pipeline prints «every number routes through fmtN()» at a commit where four surfaces do not. A system whose own checks disagree with its own screens is less coherent than one with no checks. taste 8 (held). The screens themselves are strong and the aged action queue is genuinely good work — real next actions, honest counts, correct bidi. The taste failure is one screen, not a drift. surprise 4 (up from 3). The guard is a real idea with a real insight — source over DOM — and its comment block names its own three prior failure modes, which is the opposite of the self-flattering engineering I usually have to discount. It falls short of its claim, but it is the first structural move in six rounds and it earns the point.

score_movement_ruling: I said round 19 would read ACCEPT at 9/8/8/8/4 with S6 done. S6 is done, and I am not paying out on it, because I said I would verify rather than credit the claim — and verification moved two scores the other way. Completeness cannot rise to 8 on a mechanism that covers one of ten shapes while four live counter-examples sit in the file it just cleared. Coherence has to fall when the enforcement and the screen disagree. The honest summary: the loop did the specific work I asked for, correctly and verifiably, and then over-stated what that work generalised to — which is the third consecutive round of the same over-claim and is now a rule.

demo_safety_ruling.correctness_vs_craft: Worth repeating a third round: nothing on any screen states a false fact about a customer, a campaign or a conversation. The verdicts, the evidence quotes, the counts and the funnel all reconcile. Every finding in this envelope is craft — how the product reads — except one, and that one is KB_SECTIONS, where a hardcoded «0 ملفات» is a false statement about the user's own uploaded file. That is the only correctness defect I found, and it is small.

open_items_ruling.item: No UI path to create a service
open_items_ruling.status: OPEN — unchanged, fourth round with the same ruling
open_items_ruling.reason: PRODUCTS is still a hardcoded six-service array and check-catalogue.mjs enforces it at build time (I ran it: «catalogue in step: 6 services, 0 drift»). The demo runs over the six existing services; nothing on screen invites creating one and nothing dead-ends when you do not. A real production gap, not a Thursday gap. It becomes urgent the first time a Lean salesperson wants to sell something the array does not contain.

open_items_ruling.item: Launch classification proven by code path only
open_items_ruling.reason: Proving it requires an outbound send, which user-model R5 and CLAUDE.md §5 forbid absolutely, and which he restated on 2026-08-12 in the strongest terms. open_items_ruling.item: S5 — 375px column drift on the #kmon/5 audience table (attributed to 874a130, not to these commits)
open_items_ruling.status: OPEN — unchanged, and I am ruling plainly: acceptable to carry
open_items_ruling.reason: I re-measured it at aed03a3 and the drift is exactly as I left it: at 1440 the header and row grid-template-columns are identical ('211.781 211.797 198.547 185.312 92.656 105.906'); at 375 they diverge ('76.33 71.23 55.98 25.45' header versus '61.95 68.81 45.44 52.80' row), so the four surviving column headings do not sit above their values. My geometric rect-overlap test found 0 chip-over-name collisions this run, so the visible symptom is misalignment rather than overprinting on this data. HOLD IT. Three reasons: it is pre-existing (the ≤900px rule at :209 dates to 874a130 and the diff under review contains no table CSS), it only appears below 900px on a screen he will show on a laptop or a projector, and — the reason that actually decides it — the fix is a change to a shared @media rule that governs every .thead/.trow in the product, hours before a demo, with no time to re-measure the four other tables it would touch. The right time to change a shared responsive rule is Friday, not this morning. If he demos from a phone, this moves to must and the one-line minmax(0, …) fix in round-19's S3 is still the right shape.

open_items_ruling.status: REOPENED as M2-FAIL / M6 / S1 — closed on the six audited routes, open one click below them
open_items_ruling.reason: See per_must_verification M2. The property «one numeral system» is true of every route the loop has audited and false of the first route it has not.

change_orders.order: #kb/ — the demo-blocking one. (a) src/dashboard.ts:1105: `'…tabular-nums;">' + c[1] + ""` → wrap c[1] in fmtN. Four values, 26px, the largest numbers on the screen. (b) :1147: «جاهزية الأقسام — 92%» → «جاهزية الأقسام — ٩٢٪», and do not leave a hardcoded 92 beside a computed ring — either derive it from `ready` or delete the heading's number. Verify by loading #kb/الإجازات المرضية at 1440/768/375 and counting; the target is every Latin run being a filename or a phone number, same bar as the other six routes.

src/dashboard.ts:1722 — `Math.roundfmtN(target * eased)` is not a function and it is live in production. Fix it to `fmtN(Math.round(target * eased))`. Then make a decision about countUp() rather than leaving it: it has been dead since 825a557 because parseInt strips Arabic-Indic digits to NaN. Either revive it (parse «٠-٩» before parseInt) or delete the function and its call at :1692. Do not leave a dead animation with a live TypeError in it. Whichever you choose, prove it in a browser — no static tool in this repo can see this line.

src/dashboard.ts:967 — «حد الدفعة الواحدة حاليًا 50» → «٥٠». It renders in the launch-confirm modal above «تأكيد الإطلاق ✓», four lines under «٧٠ مستهدف» in Arabic-Indic. Verify by selecting >50 contacts client-side and opening the modal, not by reading the diff.

The import-result chips, which round 19 named at :1162 and which were not done: :1162, :1209, :1230 and :1231 all concatenate d.added / d.updated / d.invalid raw. I rendered the shipped expression in the browser and it reads «أُضيف 128 حُدّث 34 غير صالح 6». This is the file-onboarding flow he asked for by name (user-model R1), so it is the second most likely defect to appear in the room after M1. Wrap all four in fmtN.

Make the guard honest and slightly wider — do NOT delete it, it earns its place. (a) Change the success message from «every number in src/dashboard.ts routes through fmtN()» to the shape it actually verifies, e.g. «no raw numeric expression is concatenated into UI text». (b) Fix blankFormatted's left boundary: /(?|%.

Move the PROPERTY assertion to where it cannot be fooled by syntax: extend scripts/smoke.py to walk the rendered DOM of every route (derived from render()'s hash dispatch, including sub-routes — that is what would have added #kb/<product>) and fail on any ASCII digit outside an allowlisted node class (direction:ltr phone spans, filenames, CSS). One runtime check that would have caught M1, M3, M4 and the numeral half of M2 in a single pass, and that grows automatically as routes are added. This is the mechanism that actually ends the series; the source guard is the fast pre-filter in front of it.

KB_SECTIONS (src/dashboard.ts:307-317, rendered at :1147-1150) is hardcoded placeholder data rendered only when the product name equals «الإجازات المرضية», and its last row asserts «0 ملفات» on a screen that shows the real attached filename 300px above. That is a false statement about the user's own upload — user-model Rule 2. Recommendation: delete the card. It is faster than fixing it, it removes three Latin numerals and one hardcoded 92, and it removes a per-product special case that will embarrass the product the moment anyone opens a different service.

The embedded seed copy on #kb/<product> — «زمن الإصدار ↓70%», «القياسية 18,000 ر.س · المؤسسات 95,000 ر.س سنويًا», «(5 أيام)، (14 يومًا)» at :292, :309, :311, :312 — renders Latin numerals in Arabic body copy on the same screen as «٩٢٪». Convert to Arabic-Indic with «٪». Lower priority than M1 because it is body type rather than display type, but it is the tail of the same screen and should go in the same pass.

Carry-over, unattempted from round 19 and still correct: resolve the «معرفة» collision on #kb and #aimkt, where a service card can show «٩٢٪ درجة معرفة المساعد» beside «بانتظار ملف المعرفة». Two different measures sharing one word reads as a contradiction. Rename the score to «اكتمال ملف الخدمة» or similar.

Carry-over, unattempted: the 375px header/row column drift on #kmon/5 (src/dashboard.ts:209, minmax(0, …) on the ≤900px grid-template-columns). Explicitly NOT before the demo — see open_items_ruling. Schedule it with time to re-measure the other tables the shared rule governs.

user_model_updates.rule: Rule 7 — The loop's own claims are subject to Rule 2. Every number, count and property assertion the loop makes ABOUT ITSELF — in evidence files, commit messages, check output and reports to the CPO — must be bounded by what was actually measured. A green check that asserts a property it does not verify is worse than no check, because the next role cites it as proof.
user_model_updates.evidence: THIRD consecutive occurrence, which meets the promotion bar. Round 18: «portal-wide numeral sweep» for a six-screen sweep. Round 19: «13 real non-zero ratios» when 12 were non-zero. Round 20, three at once: «15 comparisons, all with genuine non-zero ratios» when salespath@375 is 0.00000; «S6 shipped… ONE numeral path» when four surfaces still render Latin; and check-numerals.mjs printing «every number in src/dashboard.ts routes through fmtN()» at a commit where that is false. Note the pattern is consistently OVER-claim in the direction of completion, never under-claim — which is exactly the bias a CPO gate exists to correct.

user_model_updates.against: Rule 6, SEVENTH consecutive occurrence — rule holds; the enumeration axis rotates but the audited set never grows
user_model_updates.note: Round 19's corollary (enumerate over STATES, from the SOURCE, because a DOM count is blind to unrendered branches) was applied properly this round — all three conditional defects verified under their own triggers. And the defect moved to the axis that was NOT instructed: the route list. The six audited routes have been the same since round 17, and the defect is now on route seven, #kb/<product>, one click below #kb. Generalisation to carry, and it is the last one this shape has left: an audit's SCOPE must be derived from the system (every branch of render()'s hash dispatch, including sub-routes), never from a human's recollection of which screens were named last round. Any scope a person types by hand is a scope that freezes.

user_model_updates.against: new — extends decision 0001 (dashboard.ts: anchored replacements only, never range edits)
user_model_updates.note: Decision 0001 was written after a range edit deleted five helpers and shipped a blank page that tsc and node --check both cleared. This round an ANCHORED replacement produced `Math.roundfmtN(` — syntactically valid, type-invalid, and cleared by tsc, node --check, the new source guard, smoke's pageerror listener AND 57 QA scenarios. The rule needs its second half: anchored replacement is necessary but not sufficient, because src/dashboard.ts:247-1802 is a client <script> inside a template literal that NO static tool in this repo can parse. Any edit landing between those lines requires a runtime assertion — execute the edited surface in a browser, in the state that renders it — before it can be called done. Recommend amending .orbit/decisions/0001 rather than filing a new one.

user_model_updates.against: new — credit where it is due, recorded so the gate stays calibrated
user_model_updates.note: Three things in this round were done well and I want them on the record so the model is not purely a complaint log. (1) Every specific must from round 19 was executed correctly AND holds under its own trigger condition — I checked each by injection, and none was a paper fix. (2) The bare-toLocaleString class is genuinely dead: 1 remaining call, inside fmtN, against 76 fmtN call sites. Mechanisms do work when scoped to a shape. (3) The visual-evidence bundle has zero re-baselines for the first time — all 15 baselines predate their actuals, which I verified pairwise. The loop's evidence discipline is improving on the axis I have been pushing hardest; the failure is in the PROSE around the evidence, not the evidence.

My own miss, recorded against myself: countUp() died at 825a557 — the commit I reviewed in round 19 — because the numeral sweep made every KPI value Arabic-Indic and countUp's parseInt strips them to NaN. I passed M2 on that commit through four DOM channels and never checked whether a FEATURE that consumes those values still worked. Lesson for my own procedure, symmetric to the one I keep giving the builder: when a change alters the DATA a feature reads, re-run the feature, not just the render. A pixel-identical screen can hide a dead behaviour.

verdict_rules_applied.iterate_vs_redevelop: ITERATE, and not close to REDEVELOP. The approach is right, the mechanism is real, the execution record on named items is clean, and every open must is a small anchored edit. The gap is scope discipline, not design.
verdict_rules_applied.why_not_accept_with_a_note: Because for the first time the failure is not something I would be TELLING him about — it is something a check inside his own deploy pipeline is telling him is fine. I can ship a note that says «avoid #kb/<product>». I cannot ship a note that makes «numerals consistent: every number routes through fmtN()» true. Accepting here would ratify the claim, and the claim is the thing that keeps regenerating this defect.
verdict_rules_applied.what_would_make_this_ACCEPT: M1 and M2 done and verified in a browser, M3 and M4 done, S1's honesty fix on the guard's message. That is well under an hour of work and it reads 8/8/8/8/4.

user_impact_summary_ar:
الخلاصة: العطل المؤقّت الذي كان سيظهر اليوم الساعة ٢:٤٨ ظهرًا بتوقيت الرياض أُغلق فعليًا — تحقّقتُ منه بنفسي بتقديم الساعة في المتصفّح، وقائمة الإجراءات على الشاشة الرئيسية تقرأ الآن «٢٦ ساعة بلا متابعة» بأرقام عربية، بلا رقم لاتيني واحد. والشاشات الستّ التي سيمرّ عليها فريقك — الرئيسية، متابعة الحملات، صفحة الحملة، جهات الاستهداف، إنشاء حملة، وصفحة العميل — نظيفة عند ١٤٤٠ و٧٦٨ و٣٧٥ بكسل؛ كلّ رقم لاتيني متبقٍ فيها هو رقم جوال أو اسم ملف، وهذا صحيح.

لكنّي وجدتُ شاشة واحدة لم تُراجَع من قبل: «معرفة الخدمة» ← أي خدمة بعينها. فيها ٣٨ رقمًا لاتينيًا مقابل رقمين عربيَّين، الآن، دون أي شرط: أربعة أرقام بحجم ٢٦ بكسل («7 · 0 · 0 · 1») تحت حلقة جاهزية تقرأ «٩٢٪»، وعنوان «جاهزية الأقسام — 92%». توصيتي بوضوح: أصلِح هذين الموضعين قبل العرض — تعديلان بخمس دقائق — أو لا تفتح هذه الشاشة أثناء العرض. بقيّة المنتج جاهز.

ووجدتُ أيضًا خطأ برمجيًا حقيقيًا وصل إلى الخادم المباشر في هذا الإصدار (سطر ١٧٢٢): استدعاء لدالّة غير موجودة. أثبتُّ أنه لا يمكن أن يظهر ببياناتك الحالية، فهو ليس خطرًا على العرض — لكنّ الأهم أنّ ست فحوصات آلية مرّت عليه دون أن تراه، ومنها الفحص الجديد نفسه. الفحص الجديد مفيد ويستحق البقاء، لكنه يفحص شكلًا واحدًا من تسعة جرّبتُها، ورسالته تدّعي أكثر ممّا يتحقّق منه. طلبتُ تصحيح الرسالة وتوسيعه قليلًا.

الحكم: إعادة تكرار، بأربعة أوامر تصحيح صغيرة أقلّها الأهمّ وأسرعها. لم تُرسَل أي رسالة واتساب لأي رقم في هذه المراجعة — كل الحالات اختُبرت داخل المتصفّح فقط.
